test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which constitutional amendment gave the Directive Principles precedence over Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 39A, 43A, and 48A of the 42nd Amendment** were inserted as additional Directive Principles.
 
• By saying that "no law embodying any of the Directive Principles may be deemed unconstitutional on the grounds that it infringed any of the Fundamental Rights," the 42nd Amendment accorded the Directive Principles precedence.
 
• Laws forbidding "anti-national actions" or the establishment of "anti-national organisations" could not be declared unlawful because they infringed on any of the Fundamental Rights, according to the Amendment.
 
• The 42nd Amendment's provision that Directive Principles take precedence over Fundamental Rights was abolished by the 43rd and 44th Amendments, which also limited Parliament's ability to legislate against "anti-national actions."
 
• The 42nd Amendment also included a new section to the Constitution's Article on **"Fundamental Duties."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Arunachal Pradesh was granted statehood via the** 55th Amendment, **making it the Indian Union's 24th state.
 
• The **44th Amendment of 1978** removed the right to property from the list of fundamental rights. A new provision, Article 300-A, was added to the constitution, which provided that “no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law”.
 
• The** Forty-third Amendment of the Constitution of India**, officially known as the **Constitution Act, 1977**, repealed** six articles** that had been inserted into the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment which had been enacted by the Indira Gandhi-led Indian National Congress during the Emergency.
